dataset.name: Web Architecture & Infrastructure Knowledge Base
dataset.description: Structured semantic knowledge for understanding, designing, implementing, modifying, debugging, and verifying professional web applications and websites.
principles: Prefer semantic meaning over implementation-specific naming.
Separate conceptual entities from their implementations.
Treat aliases as synonyms, not implementations.
Treat rules as contextual unless a rule is explicitly mandatory.
Prefer the simplest architecture that satisfies the requirements.
Preserve existing architecture unless a change is required.
Verify changes at the highest relevant level.
Never assume a visual problem has only a visual cause.
Prefer relationships and dependencies over isolated knowledge.
Use diagnostics to move from symptoms to likely causes before changing code.

entities.definition: The complete software workspace containing source code, configuration, dependencies, assets, tests, and build/deployment resources.
entities.purpose: Provides the complete boundary of an application or website.
entities.why_it_exists: A project groups all resources required to develop, build, verify, and deploy the product.

placement.why_here: Project-level configuration and source directories need a common root.
avoid_locations: nested inside an unrelated application directory

rules.rule: Project-level configuration should remain centralized.
rules.exception: Framework-specific configuration may require local configuration.

security: Secrets must not be committed to source control.
anti_patterns: hardcoding secrets in source files
mixing unrelated projects in one root

verification.check: Project structure is internally consistent.
Project builds successfully.

correct: Clear separation between source, configuration, assets, and tests.
incorrect: Secrets committed directly into application source.

entities.definition: The executable web product composed of routes, pages, layouts, components, logic, data access, and infrastructure integrations.
entities.purpose: Provides the functional application experience.
entities.why_it_exists: It represents the runtime behavior users interact with.

placement.why_here: Application code belongs inside the project boundary.

rules.rule: Application responsibilities should be separated by architectural concern.
rules.exception: Very small applications may intentionally use a simpler structure.

anti_patterns: putting all application logic in one component
mixing UI rendering with unrelated infrastructure logic

verification.check: Application builds.
Application starts successfully.

correct: Pages compose components while services handle external operations.
incorrect: A single UI component directly contains all database, API, and presentation logic.

entities.definition: A URL pattern mapped to a specific application resource or page.
entities.purpose: Determines which application experience is rendered for a URL.
entities.why_it_exists: Users and systems need stable URL-based access to application resources.

placement.why_here: URL resolution belongs to routing.

rules.rule: Routes should have stable and meaningful URL structures.
rules.reason: Stable URLs improve usability, SEO, and maintainability.
rules.exception: Internal routes may use implementation-specific paths.

security: Protected routes must enforce authorization server-side where required.
seo: Public routes should use meaningful canonical URLs.
anti_patterns: duplicated route definitions
security based only on client-side route guards

verification.check: Expected URL resolves to the expected resource.

correct: /products/123
incorrect: A protected resource accessible because only the client hides the route.

entities.definition: A structural wrapper shared by multiple pages or routes.
entities.purpose: Provides persistent structure and shared UI.
entities.why_it_exists: Shared application structure should not be duplicated across pages.

placement.why_here: Layouts define structural context.

rules.rule: Shared structure should be implemented at the highest common level that requires it.

responsive_behavior: Layout must adapt to available viewport width.
anti_patterns: one giant layout containing unrelated page-specific logic

verification.check: Shared structure is consistent across applicable routes.

correct: Dashboard pages sharing a dashboard layout.
incorrect: Copying the same App Drawer markup into every dashboard page.

entities.definition: A route-level user-facing screen representing a complete application experience.
entities.purpose: Composes sections and components into a complete screen.
entities.why_it_exists: Pages provide route-specific content and behavior.

placement.why_here: Pages correspond to user-accessible application destinations.

rules.rule: A page should represent one coherent user goal or destination.
rules.exception: Complex dashboards may intentionally contain multiple workflows.

responsive_behavior: Content hierarchy must remain usable on narrow screens.
seo: Public pages should expose appropriate title and metadata.
anti_patterns: page containing all reusable component implementation inline

verification.check: Page fulfills its intended user task.
Page renders correctly across supported viewport sizes.

correct: A product detail page composed from reusable sections.
incorrect: A page with duplicated implementations of the same card component.

entities.definition: A UI mechanism that allows users to move between application destinations.
entities.purpose: Provides discoverable access to routes and application areas.
entities.why_it_exists: Users need predictable movement through the application.

placement.where: Application shell, header, App Drawer, menus, or contextual regions
placement.why_here: Navigation belongs near the content or structure it controls.

rules.rule: Navigation labels should clearly describe their destinations.
rules.exception: Icon-only navigation may be acceptable when accessible labeling is provided.

responsive_behavior: Navigation may collapse or transform on narrow screens.
Touch targets must remain usable on mobile.
accessibility: Use semantic navigation landmarks where appropriate.
Provide accessible names for icon-only controls.
anti_patterns: navigation represented only by unexplained icons

verification.check: Navigation is keyboard accessible.
Navigation destinations resolve correctly.

correct: Responsive navigation that collapses into a mobile menu.
incorrect: Desktop navigation extending beyond the mobile viewport.

entities.definition: A persistent or collapsible navigation panel used to expose major application destinations.
entities.purpose: Provides navigation for applications with multiple sections or workspaces.
entities.why_it_exists: Complex applications need persistent access to primary destinations.

placement.where: Application shell, commonly beside the main content
placement.why_here: It defines the primary navigation context.
preferred_locations: left side of desktop application shell

conditional: mobile close control when rendered as an overlay

rules.rule: The drawer should not unnecessarily consume content width on small screens.
rules.exception: Applications specifically designed around persistent navigation.

constraints.rule: Drawer must remain accessible when collapsed.

responsive_behavior: Mobile commonly uses an overlay/off-canvas drawer.
accessibility: Keyboard focus must be managed when the drawer becomes modal.
security: Navigation visibility must not be treated as authorization.
anti_patterns: using hidden navigation as a security mechanism
fixed width that exceeds narrow viewports
tradeoffs: Persistent navigation improves discoverability but consumes horizontal space.
Overlay navigation preserves content width but requires an additional interaction.

verification.check: Drawer does not create horizontal page overflow.
Drawer is keyboard accessible.
Navigation items route correctly.

correct: Desktop App Drawer becomes an off-canvas drawer on mobile.
incorrect: A 320px fixed App Drawer remains permanently visible on a 320px viewport.

entities.definition: A reusable user-interface unit responsible for a bounded visual or interactive concern.
entities.purpose: Provides reusable UI behavior and presentation.
entities.why_it_exists: Reusable components reduce duplication and improve consistency.

placement.why_here: Reusable presentation belongs in a reusable UI layer.

rules.rule: Components should have a clear responsibility.
rules.exception: Composite components may intentionally coordinate multiple concerns.

responsive_behavior: Components should adapt to their available container width.
accessibility: Interactive components must expose appropriate semantics.
Keyboard interaction must be supported where applicable.
performance: Avoid unnecessary rerenders and expensive work.
anti_patterns: god component
duplicated UI implementations

verification.check: Component behavior matches its contract.
Component renders correctly in supported states.

correct: Reusable Button component used across multiple pages.
incorrect: One component containing routing, database access, authentication, and unrelated UI.

entities.definition: An interactive control used to trigger an action.
entities.purpose: Allows users to perform commands or actions.
entities.why_it_exists: Actions require explicit interactive controls.

placement.why_here: Buttons belong near the action they perform.
avoid_locations: when navigation is the actual intent

rules.rule: Use a button when the interaction performs an action.
rules.exception: Framework abstractions may preserve equivalent semantics.

rules.rule: Use a link when the interaction navigates to another destination.
rules.exception: Framework-specific navigation abstractions may render as links.

responsive_behavior: Touch targets must remain usable on small screens.
anti_patterns: clickable div used instead of semantic button

verification.check: Button can be reached and activated with keyboard.

correct: Submit button triggering form submission.
incorrect: A div with onClick used as a button without keyboard semantics.

entities.definition: A bounded content container representing a related piece of information or action.
entities.purpose: Groups related content into a visually understandable unit.
entities.why_it_exists: Cards help organize repeated or related content.

placement.why_here: Cards group related information.
avoid_locations: content that does not benefit from visual grouping

rules.rule: Card content should represent a coherent unit.

responsive_behavior: Cards may change grid columns or width based on available space.
accessibility: Interactive cards must expose an accessible interaction model.
anti_patterns: entire card made clickable while containing incompatible nested controls

verification.check: Card remains readable across supported viewport widths.

correct: Product card containing image, title, price, and action.
incorrect: Card containing unrelated application sections.

entities.definition: A structured collection of user inputs submitted to perform an operation.
entities.purpose: Collects and validates user-provided information.
entities.why_it_exists: Many application operations require structured user input.

placement.where: Pages, dialogs, authentication screens, settings, workflows
placement.why_here: Forms belong at the point where user input is required.

rules.rule: Client-side validation should improve UX but must not replace server-side validation for trusted operations.
rules.exception: Purely local interactions with no trusted server operation.

responsive_behavior: Form controls must remain usable on touch devices.
accessibility: Validation errors must be communicated accessibly.
security: Validate and sanitize trusted server input.
Do not expose sensitive values unnecessarily.
anti_patterns: trusting client validation as security

verification.check: Valid input submits successfully.
Invalid input produces useful validation feedback.

correct: Form validates input before sending it to an API.
incorrect: Server accepts client-provided values without validation.

entities.definition: A form control used to collect a value from the user.
entities.purpose: Collects structured user input.
entities.why_it_exists: User-provided values must be captured through interactive controls.

placement.why_here: Inputs belong near the information they collect.

rules.rule: Placeholder text should not be the only label.
rules.reason: Persistent labels improve accessibility and usability.

responsive_behavior: Input should fit the available field width.
accessibility: Associate validation errors with the field.
anti_patterns: placeholder used as the only label

verification.check: Input has an accessible name.

correct: Email input with a persistent accessible label.
incorrect: Textbox identified only by placeholder text.

entities.definition: Client-side state that must be shared across multiple otherwise independent parts of an application.
entities.purpose: Coordinates shared client-side application state.
entities.why_it_exists: Some state cannot be conveniently owned by a single component.

placement.why_here: Shared state requires ownership above individual components.
avoid_locations: individual components when state is genuinely global

rules.rule: Use global client state only when multiple independent consumers genuinely require shared ownership.
rules.exception: Framework conventions may centralize certain state automatically.

performance: Avoid unnecessary global updates that rerender unrelated UI.
security: Do not treat client state as a trusted security boundary.
anti_patterns: putting every piece of local UI state into global state
tradeoffs: Global state simplifies sharing but increases coupling.
Local state reduces coupling but cannot directly coordinate unrelated components.

verification.check: All intended consumers observe correct state updates.

correct: Authenticated user context shared across application shell and pages.
incorrect: A single modal's open state stored globally without need.

entities.definition: A network-accessible interface through which an application exchanges data or commands with a service.
entities.purpose: Provides a defined interface between clients and backend capabilities.
entities.why_it_exists: Separate systems need predictable communication boundaries.

placement.why_here: Network contracts belong at a service boundary.

rules.rule: API contracts should be explicit and predictable.
HTTP APIs should be designed according to the semantics of the chosen protocol and architecture.
rules.reason: Avoids accidental or inconsistent API behavior.
rules.exception: Non-HTTP protocols may use different semantics.

rules.rule: Authentication and authorization must be enforced on trusted server boundaries.
rules.reason: Clients cannot be trusted to enforce security.
rules.exception: Public resources that intentionally require no authorization.

constraints.rule: Input from untrusted clients must be validated.
constraints.reason: Prevents malformed or malicious data from reaching trusted operations.

performance: Use pagination for large datasets when appropriate.
anti_patterns: trusting client-provided authorization
embedding database logic directly into every route handler
tradeoffs: REST is broadly interoperable but can require multiple endpoints.
GraphQL can provide flexible querying but introduces schema and operational complexity.

verification.check: Valid requests return expected responses.
Unauthorized operations are rejected.

correct: Authenticated endpoint validates input and authorizes the operation before accessing data.
incorrect: Endpoint trusts a userId supplied by the client without authorization checks.

entities.definition: A reusable application-layer unit responsible for a domain operation or external system interaction.
entities.purpose: Separates application operations from UI and transport concerns.
entities.why_it_exists: Reusable business or infrastructure operations should not be duplicated across endpoints and components.

placement.why_here: Domain operations belong outside presentation code.

rules.rule: Services should represent meaningful operations rather than arbitrary collections of unrelated functions.

security: Services operating on protected data must enforce appropriate authorization assumptions at trusted boundaries.
anti_patterns: service containing unrelated application domains

verification.check: Service operation produces expected result for valid inputs.

correct: UserService handles user-domain operations.
incorrect: One service handles users, payments, email, analytics, and unrelated UI formatting.

entities.definition: Persistent storage system used to store and retrieve application data.
entities.purpose: Provides durable data storage.
entities.why_it_exists: Application state that must survive requests or restarts requires persistent storage.

placement.why_here: Persistence belongs behind application data-access boundaries.
avoid_locations: browser storage when durable server data is required

rules.rule: Database access should normally be isolated behind an appropriate data-access boundary.
rules.exception: Very small applications may intentionally use a simpler approach.

performance: Indexes should support common query patterns.
security: Access must follow least privilege where practical.
anti_patterns: database credentials exposed to clients

verification.check: Expected records can be created, read, updated, and deleted where applicable.

correct: Server-side service accesses the database using protected credentials.
incorrect: Browser directly connects using privileged database credentials.

entities.definition: The process of establishing the identity of a user or system.
entities.purpose: Determines who is making a request.
entities.why_it_exists: Protected application functionality requires identity.

placement.why_here: Identity verification must not depend solely on untrusted client state.

rules.rule: Authentication credentials must be handled through trusted security mechanisms.

accessibility: Authentication interfaces must be keyboard accessible and clearly labeled.
anti_patterns: storing sensitive authentication secrets in unsafe client-accessible locations

verification.check: Anonymous users cannot access protected operations.

correct: Server validates the user's authenticated session.
incorrect: Client-side boolean is treated as proof of authentication.

entities.definition: The process of determining whether an authenticated identity is allowed to perform an operation or access a resource.
entities.purpose: Controls access to protected resources and actions.
entities.why_it_exists: Being authenticated does not imply permission to perform every action.

placement.why_here: Authorization decisions must be enforced where trusted resources are controlled.

rules.rule: Authorization must be enforced on trusted boundaries.

security: Verify resource ownership for resource-specific operations.
anti_patterns: hiding UI and assuming access is therefore denied

verification.check: Unauthorized users cannot perform protected operations.

correct: Server verifies that the authenticated user owns the requested resource.
incorrect: Client hides the delete button but API allows deletion for any authenticated user.

entities.definition: UI state representing an operation that has started but has not completed.
entities.purpose: Communicates ongoing work to the user.
entities.why_it_exists: Users need feedback while asynchronous work is in progress.

placement.where: Within the region affected by the operation
placement.why_here: Feedback should correspond directly to the work in progress.
avoid_locations: unrelated global regions unless the operation is global

rules.rule: Loading feedback should correspond to meaningful asynchronous work.
rules.exception: Very fast operations may not require visible loading UI.

accessibility: Loading state should be perceivable by assistive technologies when appropriate.
anti_patterns: blocking the entire application for a local operation

verification.check: Loading state ends when the operation completes or fails.

correct: Save button enters loading state during submission.
incorrect: Entire application becomes blocked while a small card refreshes.

entities.definition: UI state representing a failed operation or unavailable resource.
entities.purpose: Communicates failure and provides recovery information.
entities.why_it_exists: Users need to understand failures and what they can do next.

placement.where: Within the affected content or operation region
placement.why_here: The error should be associated with its cause.

rules.rule: Error messages should explain the problem at an appropriate level and provide recovery when possible.
rules.exception: Security-sensitive errors may require intentionally generic messages.

accessibility: Important errors should be exposed to assistive technologies.
security: Do not expose secrets, stack traces, or sensitive internal details to users.
anti_patterns: showing raw server stack traces to users

verification.check: Failure is represented and recoverable where recovery is possible.

correct: Data loading failure with retry action.
incorrect: Raw exception stack trace shown to end users.

entities.definition: Design and implementation practices that make web experiences usable by people with diverse abilities and interaction methods.
entities.purpose: Ensures application functionality is broadly accessible.
entities.why_it_exists: Users may interact through keyboards, screen readers, touch, voice, magnification, and other assistive technologies.

placement.why_here: Accessibility affects every UI layer.
avoid_locations: treating accessibility as a final isolated patch

rules.rule: Prefer native semantic HTML when it provides the required behavior.
rules.reason: Native semantics generally provide built-in accessibility behavior.
rules.exception: Custom components may be necessary when native controls cannot satisfy requirements.

anti_patterns: using ARIA to replace correct native semantics unnecessarily

verification.check: Primary interactions are keyboard accessible.
Interactive controls have accessible names.

correct: Native button used for an action.
incorrect: Clickable div with no keyboard support.

entities.definition: Practices that help public web content be discoverable, understandable, and correctly represented by search engines.
entities.purpose: Improves discoverability and search-result representation.
entities.why_it_exists: Public content often depends on search visibility.

placement.why_here: Search engines evaluate document structure and metadata.

conditional: canonical URL for indexable public pages

rules.rule: Public pages should have meaningful document titles.
rules.reason: Titles identify pages to users and search systems.

performance: Avoid unnecessary client-only rendering when discoverability depends on content availability.
anti_patterns: keyword stuffing
hiding important content solely for SEO

verification.check: Public pages expose appropriate title and metadata.

correct: Each public product page has an appropriate title and canonical URL.
incorrect: Every page uses exactly the same title.

entities.definition: Configuration controlling how application source code is transformed, bundled, validated, and prepared for execution or deployment.
entities.purpose: Produces a runnable application artifact.
entities.why_it_exists: Source code often requires compilation, bundling, transformation, or validation.

placement.where: Project root or framework-defined configuration location
placement.why_here: Build tools need project-wide configuration.

rules.rule: Build configuration should match the project's actual runtime and source structure.

performance: Build should avoid unnecessary work where practical.
security: Do not embed secrets into public build output.
anti_patterns: committing generated build output as source without a reason

verification.check: Build completes successfully.

correct: Build configuration resolves the project's entry point and dependencies.
incorrect: Static index.html added to a project that requires a package-based build runtime.

decision_rules.condition: Only one component needs the state
A small parent and its descendants need the state
Unrelated application areas need the same client state
State is primarily represented by URL parameters
State originates from a backend resource

decisions.question: Should an interaction be a button or a link?

decision_rules.condition: Logic requires secret credentials or privileged resources
Logic requires direct user interaction or browser APIs
Logic can be safely executed without browser-specific capabilities
decision_rules.preferred: server when it reduces client complexity

decisions.question: Should UI code become a separate reusable component?

decision_rules.condition: UI is reused in multiple places
UI has a clear independent responsibility
Extraction would only create unnecessary abstraction

patterns.name: Layered Architecture
patterns.description: Separates presentation, application logic, data access, and infrastructure concerns.
risks: too many abstractions for small applications
patterns.when_to_use: When the application has meaningful separation between UI, domain logic, and infrastructure.

patterns.name: Component Composition
patterns.description: Builds larger UI structures by composing smaller reusable components.
patterns.when_to_use: When UI structures contain repeated or independently meaningful concerns.

patterns.name: Responsive Adaptation
patterns.description: UI structure adapts to viewport and container constraints instead of assuming one fixed screen size.
patterns.when_to_use: For interfaces expected to operate across different viewport sizes.

patterns.name: Progressive Disclosure
patterns.description: Shows essential information first and reveals secondary complexity when needed.
risks: important information may become harder to discover
patterns.when_to_use: When the interface contains substantial optional complexity.

anti_patterns.name: God Component
anti_patterns.description: A single component owns unrelated presentation, state, business logic, data access, and infrastructure responsibilities.
anti_patterns.preferred_direction: Separate responsibilities according to actual architectural boundaries.

anti_patterns.name: Client-Only Security
anti_patterns.description: Security decisions are enforced only through client-side UI or state.
anti_patterns.preferred_direction: Enforce security on trusted server boundaries.

anti_patterns.name: Global State Everything
anti_patterns.description: All application state is placed into global state regardless of scope.
symptoms: local UI state in global store
anti_patterns.preferred_direction: Keep state at the narrowest ownership level that satisfies the requirements.

anti_patterns.name: Magic Layout Values
anti_patterns.description: Hardcoded dimensions are used without considering content or viewport constraints.
anti_patterns.preferred_direction: Use flexible sizing, constraints, and responsive adaptation.

risks: hiding overflow globally can conceal the actual bug
adding unrelated files may mask the actual architecture
changing client behavior without understanding server contract

diagnostic_rules.problem: UI displays stale or inconsistent state
possible_fixes: establish a single source of truth
move state to the correct owner

verification_rules.purpose: Detect structural and code-level problems without running the application.
Confirm the project can be transformed into a runnable artifact.
Confirm the application starts and runs.
Confirm the rendered interface matches the intended design and structure.
Confirm major interactions and content are accessible.
Confirm protected operations cannot be bypassed.
Confirm a change did not break existing behavior.

ambiguity_rules.resolution_hint: Prefer app-drawer when the element provides primary application navigation. Prefer contextual navigation when it only navigates within the current content.
Resolve using surrounding interaction and destination semantics.
Determine ownership, scope, persistence, and source before selecting the state model.

quality_rules.rule: Every entity must have a unique id.
Every entity must have a canonical_name.
Aliases must represent alternate names for the same concept.
Implementation technologies must not be stored as aliases.
Every relationship target must resolve to a known entity or explicitly defined external concept.
Rules must specify strength when they are not universally mandatory.
Security guidance must distinguish client-side UX behavior from trusted security enforcement.
Diagnostic rules should distinguish symptoms from likely causes.
Verification should identify the appropriate verification level.
Knowledge should describe concepts independently of a single framework where possible.

framework_neutrality.rule: Core conceptual entities must remain framework-neutral. Framework-specific implementations may be listed under implementations.

checks: no duplicate aliases within an entity
no framework-specific concept incorrectly represented as universal truth
